one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08. Main event: Paycom Q3 2026 results, not yet announced but by precedent after the close in the first week of November (Q3 2025 reported Nov 5, 2025 [28]) - very likely inside the window. Paycom's earnings reactions have been large this year (week of the Aug 5 Q2 report the stock went from a $165 low to a $214.94 close [5]), so I widen the monthly spread slightly to ~14% vs the 13% implied by 46%/3.5. Expectations are now high: FY27 consensus EPS rose from $12.28 to $13.95 in 60 days with 20 up / 0 down revisions [3], and Q3 consensus EPS is $2.79 vs Q2 actual non-GAAP $2.78 [2,3], so a beat is needed just to hold. Industry read-across inside the window is mixed: peers (ADP, Paylocity) report around end-Oct/early-Nov; Paychex already flagged Management Solutions slightly below plan and flat employment [7]; the Sept jobs report was weak (+29K, revisions -60K) [10] but small-business indices are stable [11,12]. Fed meets Oct 27-28 with ~84% hold priced (Kalshi/Polymarket) [14]; the September hike [13] already lifts float income above company guidance assumptions, a modest tailwind for the Q3 print and any Q4 guide. October jobs report ~Nov 6. Net: near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$233.5 (+0.5% for positive estimate-revision momentum, offset by reversal risk after an ~80% four-month run) with sigma 0.14.

Peer median forward P/E 17.1x (range 7.6x-55.3x; core payroll peers ADP 22.1x, PAYX 17.2x, PCTY 17.6x); PAYC now 17.7x [4]. bear.story: Employment turns negative (payroll prints already near zero [10]), Paycom's Feb-2027 FY27 guide disappoints (the stock traded as low as $104.90 within the past year and ~$113-125 in March-April 2026 [5]), mid-market competition (Rippling claims #1 mid-market payroll [15]) and AI-driven price pressure push revenue growth to ~4-5%; EPS ~$14.2 x 12x = $170, the low end of non-microcap peers (INTU 12.6x, BILL 12.1x).

base.story: Revenue ~7% (in line with Paylocity/ADP/Paychex 5-8% guides [6,7,8]), margins edge up, buybacks shrink shares ~5%, float income helped by the Sept hike [13]; 2028E EPS ~$15.6 x ~16x (just under peer median 17.1x) = ~$250.

bull.story: FY27 guide surprises up (revenue 9-10% as in Q2 [2]), adjusted EBITDA margin >48%, further Fed hikes (Dec hike ~73% priced [14]) lift float income, buybacks ~7%; EPS ~$16.8 x 19x (between PAYX/PCTY and ADP 22x) = ~$320. Sector consolidation (Dayforce taken private by Thoma Bravo [29]) adds a takeout floor narrative.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium taken. PAYC has the highest margin in the group (FY26 adj. EBITDA guide ~46% [2] vs Paylocity FY27 guide ~37%: $690-700M on $1.880-1.895B revenue [8]) and faster EPS growth (FY27 consensus +15% [3] vs ADP FY27 guide +9-11% [6], Paychex 3Y EPS fcst +7.5%/yr [17]), but much of the EPS growth is buyback-funded and partly debt-funded ($900M drawn [1]); revenue growth (7-8%) is similar to Paylocity; and its own history shows guide-driven drawdowns (52-week low $104.90 [5]). These offset, so a small discount to the median is used rather than a premium. Forward EV/EBITDA for peers is my derivation from StockAnalysis EV, TTM EBITDA and 3Y revenue growth forecasts; 'growth_next_yr' uses StockAnalysis 3-year forecast CAGRs because next-year figures were not available on the same page.

thesis_break_reason: $165 is ~11.8x FY27 consensus EPS ($13.95 [3]), below every non-microcap peer's forward P/E [16-27], and is where the stock traded before the Aug 5 Q2 report (week-of low $165 [5]). A sustained trade there would mean the market has thrown out the Q2 re-rating: i.e. FY27 numbers are breaking (revenue retention or new-logo sales failing, employment contraction hitting per-employee revenue, or the debt-funded buyback being paused), not ordinary 46%-vol noise.

key_uncertainties: FY2027 guidance in Feb 2027: the stock traded at $104.90-$125 in spring 2026 before the Q2 re-rating [5]; Q2 revenue grew 9.8% but the FY guide (7-8%) implies H2 deceleration [2]
US employment: Sept payrolls +29K with -60K revisions [10]; ADP guides pays per control 0-1% [6], Paylocity and Paychex assume flat workforces [7,8]
Competitive share in mid-market vs Rippling (vendor-claimed #1 mid-market payroll [15]) and AI-native entrants; only 30% of buyers raising HR tech spend [15]
Rate path: Fed hiked in Sept [13], markets price a December hike [14]; a reversal to cuts would cut float income (~$105M FY26 [2])
Leverage and buyback cadence: $900M credit facility drawn to fund $1.4B of H1 buybacks [1]; EPS growth depends on continuation
Momentum/reversal: stock up ~80% from June lows in four months [5]; consensus EPS revised up ~13% in 60 days [3]
reasoning: Lane: industry/value chain. (1) Demand backdrop from the chain: ADP guides FY27 revenue +5-6%, US pays per control 0-1% and slightly lower retention [6]; Paychex's Q1 FY27 Management Solutions grew only 4% and came in slightly below plan, with 'low fire, low hire' and flat employment assumed, but no change in competitive discounting [7]; Paylocity guides ~7% total revenue growth assuming flat client workforces [8]; Workday's HCM demand is healthy (subscription +13.9%, backlog +14.2%) [9]. Labor data are soft but not recessionary: BLS +29K with -60K revisions [10], Paychex small-business jobs index steady at 99.15 [11], ADP NER +90K with small establishments +23K [12]. Net read: industry volume growth is ~0-1% from employment, so payroll vendors grow on pricing, attach and share; Paycom's 9.8% Q2 revenue growth [2] is at the top of the peer group. (2) Rates: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% in Sept [13] and prediction markets put a Dec hike at ~73% [14], while Paylocity's guide assumed two cuts [8] - float income is a sector-wide tailwind vs guides. (3) Competition: Rippling claims the #1 mid-market payroll slot in Sapient's survey and buyers are consolidating with only 30% raising HR tech budgets [15]; this is vendor-sourced so it is used only qualitatively in the bear case. (4) Valuation: after an ~80% run since June [5] PAYC trades at 17.7x forward P/E [4], right at the 12-peer median 17.1x, and 14.0x derived fwd EV/EBITDA vs median 16.1x. With FY27 consensus EPS $13.95 [3] and my 2028E $15.62, a 16.5x P/E gives $258 and 14x EV/EBITDA gives $265; blended fair value ~$261 (+12%). (5) Distribution: three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $170/27%, base $250/48%, bull $320/25%), median ~$246, 10th-90th pct ~$155-$352 (implied vol ~32%, below the 46% trailing realized because the past year contained both a guide-shock crash and a buyback-driven re-rating; still above a typical large-cap). P(>= $232) ~0.58 reflects modest positive drift (EPS growth ~12-15%, buybacks, float tailwind) against industry volume softness, a peer-median multiple, and reversal risk after a sharp run.
